title: AMD reports third quarter sales above its guide
summary: AMD shared third quarter results after the market closed on Tuesday. A summary of its company filing says sales were $13.4 billion, higher than the roughly $13 billion it had forecast in August. Its profit per share, adjusted for one time items, was $2.09.
why: Companies give forecasts called guidance. Beating your own forecast is a good sign, but the stock price depends on whether investors hoped for even more, so the move at the open can go either way. The full report was not opened, so check the company page for details.

title: The Treasury announces how much it plans to borrow on Wednesday
summary: The U.S. Treasury scheduled its quarterly borrowing announcement for Wednesday. It tells the market how many bonds the government plans to sell in the coming months.
why: When the government sells more bonds, it may have to pay higher interest to attract buyers. Higher interest on safe bonds can make stocks look less attractive, especially fast growing ones.

title: The 10 year Treasury yield rose to 4.95%
summary: The interest rate on 10 year U.S. government bonds ticked up from 4.91% on Monday to 4.95% on Tuesday. It remains lower than the 5.05% seen on October 28.
why: The 10 year yield is like the price of borrowing money for a long time. When it goes up, new bonds pay more, so stocks have to look more attractive to compete. Fast growing companies are often the most sensitive to this.
source: U.S. Treasury daily yield curve rates
